title: Why agent governance starts with observability
summary:
Key Takeaways
- The teams we work with that ship governed agents keep a central view of every agent running across the company, so costly or unauthorized usage doesn't slip through. They also look at the full trajectory of each run, since the same agent can take different paths and call different tools on the same input.
- Both strategies depend on agent observability, the ability to record and analyze every step an agent takes. Traces show whether preventative controls like guardrails are working, and they're the foundation for detective controls that monitor agents in production.
- Problems that detective controls catch in production feed back into prevention, turning a newly discovered failure into a tighter guardrail or a new regression test.
AI applications can range from simple internal chatbots to customer-facing, mission-critical agents, but all LLM-based solutions have the capacity to reason independently, so establishing governance has become a key consideration for any degree of AI adoption. Recent headlines on agent security breaches have driven even greater urgency to set up governance as a prerequisite for AI usage and development.
While the need for agent governance is widely recognized in most organizations, most are still figuring out where to start. There is some top-down guidance on agent governance from governing bodies, such as the OWASP Agentic AI Threats & Mitigations, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, or AI Agents under EU Law. These guidelines outline agent risks, but don’t define how to mitigate these issues or verify that governance is working.
When teams we work with are shipping agents with governing standards in place, we see two main strategies in common among them:
Centralizing visibility across agents. Organizations need a central view of the agents running across the company, so costly operations, unauthorized usage, and rogue agents don't fall through the cracks. This visibility makes it possible to establish limits on agents and audit their behavior to verify that guardrails are upheld.
Understanding individual agent behavior. Agents are non-deterministic, so the same agent can take different paths and call different tools on the same input. The issues that surface are often specific to each agent's task and execution path, so teams need access to the full trajectory of each agent run to understand its actions and alert on unexpected behavior.
What is agent observability
At the core of both of these strategies is agent observability, the ability to record, inspect, and analyze every step of your AI agent takes. This typically means tracing the steps and attributes of your agent, having the ability to query and access this data readily, and leveraging capabilities to interpret the agent behavior at scale.
Observability is the cornerstone for governance strategies because a guardrail or spend/usage limit doesn't guarantee an agent will follow it, and agents need to be accurately monitored to verify that those guardrails work as intended. The metrics from observability then provide the data to continuously harden overall governance posture.
Preventive vs detective agent governance
We can think of agent governance methods at a company as either preventative or detective.
Preventative governance: Guardrails enforced at runtime to block disallowed actions, including limits, agent identity, and policies on tools, data access, models, and cost. Pre-production testing is another preventative measure, where agents are evaluated against defined quality and safety standards with a required threshold before shipping.
Detective governance: Monitoring of agent behavior quickly after execution to identify concerning actions, quality issues, and unexpected changes in behavior. These measures include online evaluations, alerts, pattern recognition, human review, and regression and drift detection.
Both types of governance depend on observability. Preventative governance relies on traces to verify guardrails work as intended and use test results to meaningfully improve agents before shipping. Detective governance uses traces to evaluate behavior, identify issues, and determine what needs to be fixed in production.
Preventative governance is verified by observability
Preventative controls start as predictions about how an agent will behave and are enforced by guardrails and gateways. These controls should be tested and gated prior to deploying to production, but also must be continuously monitored to audit that they are working as intended during agent execution.
Pre-production testing with evals and red-teaming
Pre-production testing gives teams a way to establish a quality threshold that agents must meet before they can ship. For example, a company might require every team to evaluate its agents against a golden dataset and meet a certain threshold of quality scores – like below 2% hallucination, no PII leakage, or above 90% correctness against human labels – before deployment.
A trace is the detail of an agent invocation, and trajectories are the chronological, human-readable conversational view of an AI agent session. Centralized tracing provides users with visibility into all agents being built across the organization and to confirm pre-production testing is happening to begin with, and trajectories make longer running agent actions interpretable.
After a pre-production evaluation run, its traces and trajectories describe where the agent fell on each metric. These records surface the reasons for failure and point to how to improve the agent’s behavior.
Traces also show teams where an agent needs additional guardrails. Some limits can be set before an agent runs, such as PII redaction before LLM calls or shutting down if a denylisted tool is called. Other limits are surfaced only by running evals in development, or red-teaming agents with adversarial test examples. These tests surface when an agent needs more specific guardrails, like a block on how much money a customer service agent can issue in a refund.
Production verification with traces and trajectories
Runtime guardrails are a core preventative measure, but setting these guardrails isn’t enough to confirm that they are working each time an agent runs. Before the agent is shipped, teams need audibility in place to confirm that these guardrails work every time an agent is invoked, and ways to explain what happened when they fail.
Tracing and trajectories are critical for recording and understanding the agent’s behavior in production, and function as an audit trail for regulators, security bodies, and teams to confirm that guardrails are in place or investigate when guardrails have been bypassed.
Audibility is key because agents may find alternative ways to reach a goal that involve undesirable intermediate steps, sometimes known as “gaming” the path to a desired end state, in ways that didn’t appear in pre-production testing. For example, an agent without write access to a database might reach the same table through a sandbox, or a support agent with a refund approval limit might split one large refund into two smaller ones to bypass it. Subtle changes to the agent, like model drift or tool failures, can exacerbate these effects.
Detective governance is built on observability
Detective governance uses the observed agent behavior to check if agents are operating within an organization's specific standards, set agent-level quality checks, identify and alert on violations or degradation, and trigger improvements when needed. These operations all depend on being able to inspect and analyze agent traces in production.
Online evaluations, dashboards, and alerts
Online evaluations run automatically over live traces to score agent behavior against quality and safety standards. They can catch issues like PII leakage, excessive tool-calling loops, and exposed secrets, as well as domain-specific failures. For example, a customer service agent handling refund requests could be evaluated on whether it verifies a customer's identity and checks order details before issuing a refund.
Dashboards bring signals like evaluation scores, failure patterns, error rates, latency, cost per run, and behavioral trends together, giving teams visibility into agent quality, safety, reliability, and operational performance over time. With a more granular view, teams can identify emerging issues, investigate root causes, and understand whether changes improve performance.
Alerts turn these metrics into actionable items. For instance, teams can set thresholds on qualitative evaluation scores such as PII leakage occurrences or hallucinations, and operational metrics such as error rates, retries, or cost.
These capabilities, which run on top of the metadata from traces or evaluation computed on an agents’ trajectory, help teams identify concerning behavior as it happens and route issues to the right people for review and remediation.
Identify patterns and drift across agent traces
Certain agent degradations or risks only become evident when inspecting patterns among traces.
In the customer support agent’s case, the conversations may start involving requests outside the agent’s original scope. While the agent may decline politely without raising an error, satisfaction would drop in that specific category while barely affecting the overall satisfaction rate. In this scenario, a single trace may look correct without an error, but by comparing and clustering behavioral patterns, the satisfaction drop for a particular topic would be evident.
Observability tools like LangSmith Insights reports automatically cluster large volumes of trace data into common agent behaviors, failure modes, and specified metrics, helping teams identify issues that individual evaluations or alerts may miss.
Regression and drift detection also help teams determine whether changes to an agent introduce new failures or degrade previously reliable behavior. Offline evaluations run against datasets built from reviewed traces that represent correctly handled cases. Teams can test the agent against the same dataset daily to detect regression and drift, or test new agent configurations against these datasets to compare evaluation scores before and after a change.
Categorizing trends at scale also helps identify when a shared change affects several agents at once, allowing teams to catch risks before they become larger production issues.
Diagnose and review
Evaluations and alerts can identify concerning behavior, but they cannot anticipate every failure mode. In non-deterministic systems, the issue space is large and open-ended, and agents can degrade as their context, tools, and operating conditions change, even when the agent itself has not been modified.
Human review helps teams investigate cases where automated checks are insufficient. Domain experts can audit flagged traces, score agent behavior, and promote correctly handled examples into reference datasets for ongoing testing.
In our customer service agent example, reviewers might inspect conversations where the agent declined out-of-scope requests to understand whether it handled them appropriately.
Observability makes this process more manageable by surfacing the runs most relevant for review, such as those with low correctness scores or flagged actions, rather than requiring reviewers to inspect thousands of traces manually.
Traces also contain signals about failures and governance breaches that existing evals, guardrails, or alerts can miss. However, manually reading production traces at scale is often impractical, so teams need ways to surface these problems automatically from trace signal.
LangSmith Engine can analyze traces to identify recurring failures, propose fixes, and test them against the traces associated with the issue. The customer service agent may repeatedly attempt to call a non-existent tool when handling a particular type of refund request. Engine can help identify this recurring behavior

title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
summary: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. title: Public-Private Cooperation in the Port of Rotterdam: An Agent-Based Toy Model of Cooperative Efforts Against Cocaine Trafficking
summary: Cocaine trafficking poses a persistent governance challenge in the Port of Rotterdam (PoR), requiring cooperation between public and private actors. This paper develops an Agent-Based toy Model (ABM) coupled with a Causal Loop Diagram (CLD) to explore interactions between trust, cooperation, competition, pressure, enforcement, and actor skills in public-private cooperation (PPC). Based on empirical data of PPC in the PoR, we explore responses to parameter shocks across different initial configurations. In this model, effectiveness of PPC is strongly state-dependent and measures institutional, relational, behavioral, and resource readiness. The toy model demonstrates that isolated, single-track measures yield limited long-term gains modelled over 5 years due to structural system inertia, whereas coordinated multi-parameter strategies produce substantial improvements. Specifically, combining trust-building, cooperation, and moderate pressure with reduced regulatory enforcement friction raises effectiveness by 25% from a baseline effectiveness, compared to just 13% for an isolated increase in cooperation. Acknowledging the exploratory nature of the model, these findings offer exploratory hypotheses on port security governance. Future work should validate the model against test cases and additional expert input.

title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)
summary: The global deployment of autonomous AI agents within and across organisations exceeds the governance infrastructure available to constrain it. Agent communication and authentication protocols, principally the Model Context Protocol and the Agent2Agent Protocol, are maturing quickly, but maturity at the protocol layer does not produce legal legibility at the governance layer. Runtime enforcement written by the deploying organisation fixes the resources an AI agent can reach, not the authority under which it acts. Legal legibility is the capacity of a legal system to recognise, interpret and regulate activity by mapping it onto legal personhood, property, rights and liabilities. Existing (analogue) legal infrastructure cannot supply it for autonomous deployment. The resulting deficit is bidirectional. It concerns the attribution of liability when an AI agent causes harm, and the allocation of rights, including data and economic rights, generated by agentic activity and by the AI agent itself as a source of value and form of property. This paper characterises that deficit as the legal attribution gap, a material and unaddressed risk to economies, organisations and citizens that is magnified in cross-organisational multi-agent deployment. The paper describes the Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA), in which AI systems and data assets are registered as legal objects anchored to one or more identified legal persons, governed by cryptographically tethered smart legal instruments and evaluated at runtime. Each smart legal instrument can carry a legal context clause, through which the legislation, regulation and judicial decisions in force at the time of the act are given practical and legal effect in that evaluation. Infrastructure of this kind is a precondition for the continued function of any legal, property and economic system with both human and autonomous machine stakeholders.

title: Evolving Decoding Algorithms for Quantum Error Correction
summary: Quantum computation entails robustness engineering: a noisy quantum state is measured continuously, and a classical algorithm (the decoder) must infer corrections that reliably remove the noise, fast enough to keep up. We write several published belief-propagation (BP) decoders for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes in a Domain-Specific Language (DSL), and search over it with grammatical evolution. Written in the language, the published decoders show their parameters in plain view, allowing us to re-parameterise BP+OSD (ordered statistics decoding) and BP+LSD (localized statistics decoding) decoders with damping, before any search, making each 17.1--41.0$\times$ faster at a higher error rate, and BP+OSD-0 about 103 faster than the ldpc package's version tuned on the [[72,12,6]] bivariate-bicycle code. Evolution over the language finds decoders that improve the time-error front. One makes 23% fewer logical errors than BP+OSD-0 with damping at 0.64$\times$ its time, and decoders evolved from random code are more accurate than ldpc's tuned BP+OSD-0 at 1/31 of its time or less. Frozen at one operating point, the two fastest evolved decoders generalize well across noise levels, code sizes and round counts, staying at the time-error front. Ultimately, we demonstrate that capturing expert knowledge within a DSL creates a powerful intermediate layer---one that effectively bridges human intuition and machine-driven optimization to unlock highly efficient quantum error correction.

title: Coherent belief and opinion propagation produces more echo chambers: corrected version
summary: The occurrence of echo chambers is a well-known phenomenon in social networks. Echo chambers are groups of agents satisfying three properties: homogeneity, i.e., sharing the same opinion, segregation, i.e., listening primarily to agents of the same group, and reinforcement, i.e., increasing opinion similarity over time. Opinion dynamics models have been used to explain how echo chambers occur through agents updating their opinions. However, social network users also exchange beliefs supporting their opinions. Here, we aim at identifying the effect of propagating beliefs together with opinions on the formation of echo chambers. For that purpose, we complement an existing opinion dynamics model with classical belief merge operations. Beliefs and opinions are also maintained coherent guided by values that agents share. We introduce measures, applying to either beliefs and opinions, to identify echo chambers based on the three properties. This model is used to simulate opinion and belief propagation with varying initial conditions and agent tolerance for different opinions/beliefs. Results confirm the occurrence of echo chambers observed in previous opinion dynamics studies in a different setting and with a stricter measure. They also demonstrate the occurrence of echo chambers with belief propagation. Finally, they show that connecting opinions to beliefs and maintaining their coherence increases the number of belief echo chambers, but that they involve a reduced number of agents.

title: Interlacing Committees with Edge-Expansion
summary: Approval-based committee selection has recently been studied through the lens of \emph{interlacing}, a framework for studying polarization in approval elections, in which committees induce a similarity graph over voters. The quality of committees is then evaluated through the connectivity of the resulting graph. We revisit the connectivity measures used in this framework and propose \emph{edge-expansion}, a classical graph-theoretic measure with well-established connections to polarization in networks, as the optimization objective. We provide a theoretical foundation for this proposal by relating interlacing to classical models of information diffusion and by comparing edge-expansion with previously proposed connectivity objectives, identifying qualitative differences in the structural properties they capture. Finally, we study the computational complexity of optimizing edge-expansion, showing that hardness persists even for voter-interval preferences, while the problem is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed committee size, with an improved dependence on the committee size for voter-candidate-interval preferences.

title: DS2Agent: Holistic Device Agents for Accelerated Embedded Board-Level Design
summary:
Embedded board-level development demands extensive expertise, from component selection and device characteristics to interface configuration, driver writing, and system composition. Recently, LLM-based agents have shown strong capabilities, raising the prospect of automating board-level design tasks. However, existing agents either target chip-level design or treat datasheets as static text, offering little guidance on whether a specific component should---or even could---be used for a given board-level design. Moreover, without touching real hardware, they hallucinate incorrect details.
To fill this gap, we present {\setlength{\fboxsep}{1pt}\href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DS2Agent-9FE8/}{\fcolorbox{blue}{white}{DS2Agent}}}, an open-source framework that constructs interactive agents from device datasheets. Each agent comprises three models: a knowledge model supporting retrieval and question answering; a digital-twin model capturing the physical functionality of the device; and an interface model supporting driver development and system integration. To suppress hallucinations, we also allow optional connections to real devices, so that the agent can calibrate its internalized knowledge against the device. We evaluate DS2Agent on ten devices spanning seven functional categories. Compared with the baseline, the DS2Agent-augmented agent improves the question-answering score from 87 to 97 out of 100 while using 44.8\% fewer tokens. For driver generation, it reduces average token usage per device by 72.9\%. For system integration, it reduces total token usage across three FreeRTOS applications by 29.7\%.

title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
summary: Large Language Models show great potential for automated Register-Transfer Level repair, yet they struggle with non-local faults where root causes and failing outputs reside far apart in source code. Treating RTL as a flat token sequence obscures hardware dataflows, whereas exposing complete synthesized graphs overwhelms the model with fine-grained metadata. To resolve this representation dilemma, we propose GRODE-RTL, an anchor-centric representation that extracts the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, maps netlist nodes back to editable source lines, and organizes them into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. By prioritizing direct drivers and folding distant hops, GRODE-RTL guides standard tool-using agents without exposing ground-truth hints or oracle feedback. We evaluate GRODE-RTL across 30 formally validated non-local faults using three LLMs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, and MiniMax-M3) alongside a controlled six-configuration ablation study. GRODE-RTL improves pass@1 over source-level exploration by 16.7% on DeepSeek, by 26.7% on GLM-5.2, and by 20.0% on MiniMax-M3, with consistent gains on the hard-to-retrieve far-distance and indirect-anchor subsets of all three models. Our controls isolate structural relevance from generic context expansion, proving that selective dependency organization rather than full graph exposure is key to effective RTL repair.

title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing
summary: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? Such a connection would make the intended division of labor inspectable before training and allow the allocation itself to guide inference. We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. Players choose positions to maximize their expected shares of the prompt distribution, without using expert losses. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. We evaluate InflEns on a corpus assembled from seven safety-related benchmarks, which demonstrates that the highest-share expert has the lowest held-out response negative log-likelihood (NLL) on approximately 90% of prompts across four kernels under a sharpened simplex representation, compared with approximately 15% after permuting allocations across prompts. We demonstrate that the method performs comparably to published learned gates without having to train an explicit gate on the experts. Because the router is fixed, we can trace harmful behavior to a single expert and retrain only that expert, which lowers HarmBench attack success from 0.51 to 0.02 while keeping instruction following. The game also gives us several controls over how the experts specialize, including the kernel choice and its parameters, the trait-space geometry, and the number of experts. Importantly, InflEns is a general framework that can be extended to any encoder and data distribution.

title: GridAnchor: Specialized Multi-Agent AI for Safeguarding Autonomous Energy Systems Against Cyber-Physical Hallucinations
summary: Autonomous energy systems increasingly chain specialized learned agents, such as a forecaster, a state estimator and a dispatcher that may be a language model. These agents can emit confident outputs that contradict physics, and downstream agents may act on them. We define such cyber-physical hallucinations and their cascades, organize them in eight types, and build CPH-Bench, a generator of labeled episodes on SimBench feeders. We propose GridAnchor, a verification layer whose Physics-Residual Graph Transformer scores every claim from residuals between the claims, the measurements and a linearized grid model. Mondrian conformal p-values with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure turn the scores into decisions, a root head attributes cascades, and a quadratic program repairs unsafe actions with a voltage margin calibrated at repaired steps. On a simulated rural medium-voltage feeder, GridAnchor reaches a message-level area under the precision-recall curve of 0.846, against 0.837 for the strongest of six baselines, a difference within the confidence interval. It leads on estimates and actions, whereas a self-consistency check that knows the label tolerances reaches 0.874 by leading on forecasts. The false-alarm rate stays within 0.17 percentage points of the nominal level on steps without injected hallucinations. In closed loop, GridAnchor leaves no bus outside the voltage band on the test days, against 0.0700% of the bus-steps without protection, and simpler detectors with the same mitigation come close. Stale but coherent messages and single-bus forecast errors remain mostly undetected.

title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
summary: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.

title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
summary: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.

title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations. All data are generated by a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that combines grasp generation, motion planning, and closed-loop throw optimization under randomized physical properties. We evaluate three representative VLAs, GR00T N1.7, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA, and find that all achieve success rates below 3\%. Our analysis reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success. Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns. We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.

title: ACE-Brain-0.7: Learning Execution-Grounded Reasoning for Embodied Agents
summary: Reliable reasoning for long-horizon embodied tasks requires predictions grounded in the observed execution state. We present ACE-Brain-0.7, a 9B vision--language model that combines spatial grounding, task understanding, and progress estimation. To train the model, we curate 3.7 million question--answer pairs, drawing execution supervision from egocentric human videos, robot episodes, and simulation. These questions span different stages of an execution and connect task-level judgments with observed progress and outcomes. We then fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this collection together with additional task, spatial-grounding, and progress-estimation data. Across six public task-reasoning benchmarks, ACE-Brain-0.7 achieves an average score of 76.5, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 72.7 and Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.5. Our model also leads the evaluated models in spatial grounding, averaging 75.90 across seven benchmarks and reaching 91.25 Acc@0.5 on RefCOCOg. Controlled evaluations further indicate that our task-only model makes more effective use of visual history and more accurately distinguishes execution states. Together, these results show that ACE-Brain-0.7 effectively combines spatial perception with temporal understanding, delivering strong execution-grounded reasoning and comparing favorably with closed-source models.

title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
summary: Power electronics is central to the energy transition, but developing new hardware still relies on human-led design, fabrication, testing, and iteration. We present JARVIS, an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes this loop for circuit boards. JARVIS maintains machine-specific capabilities and constraints, scans its workspace using a robot-mounted 3D scanner, and constructs an executable digital twin in which it rehearses robot motions, fabrication steps, and circuit behavior before consuming materials. A single text instruction initiates the physical experiment. Using unmodified desktop equipment, the agent coordinates a robot arm, a PCB printer that deposits conductive silver ink and solder paste, and a pick-and-place machine. It verifies progress using cameras and sensors, then tests the fabricated circuit with an OPAL-RT real-time simulator and an oscilloscope. Based on the measurements, JARVIS diagnoses deviations from the design and generates a revised design in KiCad for subsequent rehearsal. In a demonstration involving a 60 Hz notch filter for grid-connected converter sensing, JARVIS completed a first-run experiment in 2 h 39 min without human intervention, achieving 50.6 dB attenuation at 60 Hz. Its digital-twin rehearsal identified five issues before fabrication, including a test criterion that would have incorrectly rejected a functioning board. During execution, the agent also resolved encountered faults autonomously. These results demonstrate an integrated agent-driven workflow for physical design, fabrication, measurement, and iterative improvement of power-electronic circuitry. To our knowledge, JARVIS is the first system in power electronics in which an agent closes the physical design-build-test-learn loop for circuit boards.

title: An Open-Source ROS 2 Framework for Shared Control in Surgical Teleoperation: Integrating the Haply Inverse3 with the da Vinci Research Kit
summary: Surgical teleoperation deprives surgeons of touch, forcing visual inference of tissue forces; the commercial platforms now restoring force feedback remain closed, preventing open research on haptic shared control. This paper provides a system contribution: it presents an open-source, ROS 2-native framework that integrates the compact, three-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) Haply Inverse3 haptic device with the da~Vinci Research Kit (dVRK). The framework includes a novel mapping strategy that combines 3-DOF translational device input with separately tracked VerseGrip orientation into 6-DOF patient-side manipulator commands. Two virtual-fixture-inspired guidance modes serve as reference implementations to evaluate the framework in a within-subjects user study on a teleoperated hot-wire benchmark task in simulation, and the architecture is further demonstrated on physical dVRK hardware. Relative to unassisted manual control, linear guidance significantly reduced both the number of wire contacts and the task completion time, whereas the progressive-stiffness guidance produced consistent but statistically non-significant trends in the same direction. Subjective ratings of workload, agency, and satisfaction showed favorable descriptive trends for the guidance modes. The results demonstrate the feasibility of haptic shared control with a compact device coupled to the dVRK and provide an openly available, reproducible platform for future research. They further suggest that simpler linear feedback may be more robust for inexperienced operators than more complex profiles.

title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
summary: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.

title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
summary: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

title: Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
summary: Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds. Notably, the fractional part of this charge is insensitive to local perturbations of the dislocation core, and it therefore persists after the in-gap core state is removed, as we show analytically in the chain limit and numerically away from it. In the Weyl-semimetal counterpart, the response to a magnetic flux separates this crystalline charge from the charge set by the Chern number of each momentum slice. We propose that a half-integer core charge that persists after the in-gap peak disappears from the local spectrum can be detected in artificial electronic and optical lattices, with metamaterials providing complementary access to the core modes.

title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.

title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
summary: Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. We embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CKAN) in finite element model updating (FEMU) and train it by minimizing the mismatch between the predicted and the measured kinematic fields and reaction forces. Pruning and symbolic regression then reduce the trained network to a compact closed-form strain energy that satisfies every constitutive requirement. On perforated natural-rubber membranes, the CKANs reproduce the DIC displacement fields with median errors between one and two percent, and transfer to a hole pattern withheld from training. On a perforated silicone plate, a CKAN trained on one stretch profile at a single load reproduces that profile and the measured reaction force to within a few percent. On an aortic specimen inflated under pressure, an anisotropic CKAN predicts the inflated three-dimensional shape. The discovered closed-form energies match the CKANs they replace on the training data and can be compared directly with established models.

title: Two distinct notions of speed in antiferromagnets
summary: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available. In insulating NiO, restricted electronic scattering channels reduces the ultrafast response. Our results distinguish ultrafast demagnetization from exchange-enhanced precession and identify the interplay of spin-flip probability and electronic scattering rate as a key factor governing the nonequilibrium response of compensated magnets.

title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
summary: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
summary: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4). Analysis based on the Wiedemann-Franz law indicates a modest increase in electron transport (~5%) and a significant increase in phonon transport (~100%) after HPT processing. The phonon mean free path remains small on the order of 0.6-1.1 nm, and comparison with the Cahill-Pohl model shows that heat transport occurs near the minimum thermal conductivity limit, where vibrational modes are strongly scattered. This suggests that the enhancement in thermal transport is not governed by conventional defect scattering, but it is hypothesized that modifications in atomic-scale disorder, such as deformation-induced short-range ordering, are responsible for this unusual behavior. Specific heat capacity increases after HPT, consistent with stored defect energy. The linear thermal expansion exhibits a non-monotonic behavior, decreasing initially due to internal stresses and relaxation effects, and increasing at higher strains due to grain boundary-induced anharmonicity. These findings highlight the complex interplay between defects, atomic-scale disorder, and nanostructure in governing the electrical and thermal properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys via electron and phonon scattering.

title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
summary: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere. For example, the preferences favor KCo2As2 and CoGa, reported compounds with partially flat bands that the score would discard. The framework also extends to synthesizability and phonon properties. Our findings suggest that reward misalignment can expose opportunities for materials discovery beyond what fixed rewards are designed to find.

title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
summary: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

title: Lattice dynamics study of (Bi1-xSbx)2Te3 compounds: Comparative compositional study of force constants and Grüneisen parameters
summary: We performed a comprehensive Raman spectroscopy study of (Bi1-xSbx)2Te3 (BST-x) compounds, with varying Sb concentration, under ambient and high-pressure conditions. At ambient conditions, the frequency of all observed Raman-active modes (E1g, A11g, E2g, A21g) is blue-shifting with increasing Sb concentration, albeit with varying concentration-dependent rate. Based on these results, we calculated the relative force constants as a function of Sb concentration using a harmonic approximation, which shows a mode-dependent variation. The force constants for the lower frequency Raman modes (E1 g and A11g) remain almost composition-independent, while for the higher-frequency ones a profound softening (E2g) or stiffening (A21g) was determined. From the Raman spectroscopy measurements under high-pressure conditions, the corresponding Grüneisen parameters for the three observed Raman-active modes (A11g, E2g, A21g) as a function of composition were determined by combining them with the previously reported Equation of States and the corresponding bulk modulus B0 of the ambient-conditions R-3m phase. The average Grüneisen parameter exhibits a clear maximum for BST-07. Based on Slack's equation, these results are directly related to the optimal ZT values for this composition. Our study provides a solid framework for connecting composition, lattice dynamics, and thermal-transport behaviour, towards establishing the microscopic origin of thermoelectric optimization in BST compounds.

title: Process-Knowledge-Guided Latent Diffusion for Generative Design of Porous Architectures: A Case Study in Aerosol Jet Printing
summary: Printed porous layouts interleave functional material with open channels, and the layout that uses the material best depends on how the process settings shape the deposit. Generative models propose layouts quickly, but a generator that does not receive the process setting samples from the same distribution at every setting, even when the process-dependent score ranks candidate layouts differently. This paper examines whether process knowledge can steer a latent diffusion generator toward layouts suited to a given process setting in a prescribed design domain. We formulate a process-dependent utilization score in which a process model sets the length over which the utility of printed material decays with distance from a channel. The generator combines a vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) latent representation, a topology U-Net, a ControlNet domain branch, and a separately trained regressor that predicts the score from noised latents; the domain branch conditions each denoising step and the regressor gradient steers it. The method is applied to aerosol jet printing, where the atomizer and sheath gas flows enter the score through the flow-focusing relation. Across seven modeled flow settings, the lowest-scoring candidate layout of a domain differed between settings in 191 of 500 domains. In a sampling study, the mean directly computed score on three validation domains and one test domain was 0.642 with domain conditioning alone, 0.636 at a weight of 300, and 0.450 at 12,000 (112 scores per weight; lower is better). The results support process-knowledge-guided generation as an approach to process-specific porous design under the stated assumptions.

title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
summary: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise. The theory makes five claims: value is governed by calibration rather than by activity, speed, agreement, or tenure; calibration leaves observable traces in behavioral telemetry; those traces are non-diagnostic on their own, because the fast, low-revision signature of a calibrated expert is indistinguishable from that of a confident novice until it is gated by outcomes; human calibration and a model's self-knowledge are the same construct, so the joint system should defer to whichever agent is better calibrated on each item; and individual calibration is causally identifiable only above the level of the single judgment. We ground each claim in a six-month production window of an AI-assisted accounting system (541621 reviewer events, 483 reviewers), and find that a purely behavioral expertise profile inverts the ground truth, scoring an overconfident cohort (5.2 percent correction survival) higher than genuine experts (99.2 percent); that reviewer quality is flat across tenure, so the trait is not learned on the job; and that the same calibration logic that separates good from bad reviewers, applied to the model, concentrates 92.5 percent of human effort on genuine errors. We close with the boundary the theory must respect: under majority-vote aggregation, individual causal value is unidentifiable.

title: Beyond corridor averages: Lane-level validation of microscopic freeway simulation with empirically parameterized arrivals
summary: Traffic flow modeling is an essential part of civil planning around the world, and traffic simulation is an important component of the analyses that city planners must perform to ensure safe and efficient road networks for their citizens. This work advances microscopic traffic simulation through lane-level validation of speed and flow dynamics, addressing a critical gap in conventional macro-aggregated approaches. We systematically evaluate the trade-offs between numerical integration methods and vehicle arrival processes when reproducing empirical trajectory data from California's freeway network. Results demonstrate that numerical-integrator choice has negligible impact on simulation accuracy, with less than one percent variation across eight methods, while vehicle arrival-process modeling substantially affects fidelity. The shifted Erlang-2 distribution reduces flow-prediction error by approximately 28% compared to Poisson processes by enforcing a realistic minimum headway. Lane-level validation across five detector stations reveals lane-specific dynamics that aggregated metrics often obscure.

title: LAaDT-DSS: decision support for non-experts on rooftop PV, incentive and grid simulations under Turkish tariff rules
summary: Rooftop photovoltaics raise three questions: should a household invest, which incentive costs the state least, and does the feeder stay within limits? Those who ask are rarely modellers. We present LAaDT-DSS, decision-support software that answers all three under Turkish tariff rules from one simulation core. Non-experts reach it by clicking a house on a 3D map or by asking in plain words; a language model is asked to call the simulation tools, not to compute. Each entry of its 125-entry parameter registry is marked as sourced or estimated. Case studies test the system. Its PV yield lies within $\pm$3.6% of two independent tools at equal losses. Across 2,048 draws of its estimated inputs, the answer for PV alone held in all but one; with a battery, it changed in 31-41% of the draws. Four scripted chat scenarios ran end to end; no user study was run.

title: Uneven gains in protein-RNA affinity and mutation-effect prediction
summary: Accurate matched affinities determine mutation effects, but gains in aggregate affinity prediction may transfer unevenly to average effects, ordering and local accuracy. We evaluated eleven method families using method-specific matched populations. Controlled CoPRA reduced absolute-affinity mean absolute error from 1.2898 to 1.1431 pKd. Across 220 mutation pairs from 20 families, it generated stronger responses and improved mean-effect accuracy, with uncertain ranking gains and no decrease in mean centered local error. In an independent external test (24 quantitative pairs from three source-matched families), absolute and ordinary mutation-effect errors fell in all three families. Mean centered local error fell from 0.4198 to 0.3761 pKd, with improvements in two families and higher error in one. Error decomposition localized gains in landscape means. PRA-Pred feature tracing, fixed-weight M2-PRNet input controls and matched supervision interventions identified specific restrictions on mutation response. These results establish the need to evaluate average effects, ordering and quantitative local variation jointly.

title: CHORUS: Cross-Subject Harmonization via Population Relay for Unseen Subjects in Brain Visual Decoding
summary: EEG-based image retrieval performs well on training subjects but generalizes poorly to unseen individuals. Existing calibration methods address this gap by aligning a new subject directly with image embeddings. We find that the training population is a better alignment target: an unseen subject's embeddings are closer to the stimulus-matched population average than to the image embeddings, and the remaining gap to the population is largely a shift and a rotation. Motivated by this finding, we propose CHORUS. At training, stimulus-matched cross-subject averaging (SCA) teaches the encoder to match responses to the same image across subjects; at deployment, a two-stage calibration first aligns an unseen subject to population anchors predicted from the decoder's visual features, and then to the image embeddings. On leave-one-subject-out THINGS-EEG2 with two backbones, CHORUS improves over direct calibration by 10.92 and 6.63 points on unlabeled test batches and by 4.2-6.9 points with 10-200 labeled pairs; even without the population stage, SCA and direct calibration each outperform prior training and calibration schemes. The complete system reaches 78.37% and 73.40% 200-way Top-1 accuracy, 36.32 and 20.93 points above SCORE.

title: The Partially Saturated Cells Method for Complex Moving Geometries in Turbulent Flow Conditions
summary: We present four application cases to test and validate fluid-structure-interaction models based on the Lattice Boltzmann and the Partially Saturated Cells method (PSM) for turbulent flow conditions. For a flow around a stationary sphere we compare the PSM with direct mapping boundary conditions and achieve good agreement to reference data for Reynolds numbers up to one million. In particular, the model predicts the drag crisis for this case with good accuracy. For a three dimensional airfoil simulation at a Reynolds number of 150000, the PSM predicts the stall angle for a NACA0018 profile with excellent accuracy. For a geometry-resolved stirred tank simulation at a Reynolds number of 29000 the PSM produces the time averaged velocity profiles around the impeller with excellent fidelity. Finally, a wind turbine geometry is resolved with the PSM for a tip Reynolds number of 40000, where thrust and mean velocity in the turbine wake shows excellent agreement with reference data from literature.

title: MetacouplingLLM: Integrating geographic adjacency, flow indicators, and LLM-assisted analysis
summary: The metacoupling framework examines interactions within coupled human and natural systems and between adjacent or distant systems, but its application is constrained by inconsistent geographic classifications and limited standardized quantitative workflows. We present MetacouplingLLM, an open-source Python package integrating adjacency databases, reproducible flow indicators, and large language model (LLM)-assisted qualitative analysis. The databases combine administrative boundaries, hydrography, and fixed-crossing evidence, with configurable adjacency policies and optional country-level maritime adjacency. Metacoupled Flow Shares, Metacoupled Flow Evenness, and the Metacoupled Flow Concentration Index characterize flow composition, balance across coupling types, and partner concentration within each type. The qualitative workflow combines literature retrieval, optional web evidence, and geographic checks to draft structured analyses. Applications to global marine fishing and Indonesian palm oil demonstrate these capabilities; the fisheries reanalysis reveals differing partner concentration among regions with similar telecoupled flow shares. MetacouplingLLM facilitates consistent framework application and comparative sustainability research.

title: Pinterest 联合英特尔将开源性能分析推向互联网级规模
summary:
Pinterest 与英特尔合作对 gProfiler 进行功能扩展。这是一款开源的持续性能分析工具，能够为互联网规模的基础设施集群提供生产环境性能可见性。
Pinterest 运维着数十万个实例，为 6.4 亿月活跃用户提供支撑，业务服务采用 Java、Python、C++、Go 和 Node.js 编写。在这样的规模下，即使是很小的效率提升也会带来显著的基础设施和成本影响。工程师此前使用 perf、async-profiler 和 py-spy 等工具，生成的性能分析数据是碎片化的，很难跨语言、跨机器进行关联分析。
Pinterest 没有自研一套闭源性能分析平台，而是联合英特尔扩展 gProfiler，并将新增能力回馈给该开源项目。本次合作新增了动态分析、硬件层遥测、挂钟时间分析、性能计数器火焰图等能力，同时针对大型生产集群对系统做了稳定性加固。
gProfiler 作为多个现有性能分析工具的编排层。它将系统级的 perf 数据与运行时专用工具（如用于 Java 的 async-profiler、基于 eBPF 的 Python 性能分析）相结合，针对单台主机上运行的全部进程生成统一的火焰图。
这一点对于现代服务来说尤为重要，因为应用的执行会跨越多个层级。一个 Java 应用可能将时间消耗在 JVM 内部、本地库或 Linux 内核中，而 Python 服务则可能涉及解释器、本地代码和内核活动。gProfiler 将这些视图整合在一起，而不是要求工程师手动选择并关联不同的性能分析工具。
这个代理会自动发现进程、启动相应的性能分析器、合并它们的堆栈跟踪信息，并上传生成的性能分析数据，全程无需修改应用程序代码。
新的能力让工程师能够通过 UI 或 API 选择服务、主机或集群，并远程触发性能分析。代理平时处于休眠状态，CPU 占用低于 1%，内存占用约 100 MB，并通过定时心跳接收性能分析指令。你可以在不重新部署代理的情况下修改性能分析的频率、时长和所使用的分析器。
这就把性能分析转变为一种运维能力，不再要求工程师获取单台机器的 shell 访问权限。
通过与 Intel PerfSpect 集成，gProfiler 能够收集硬件级信息，如缓存行为、内存带宽和 CPU 停顿。Pinterest 还增加了 PMC 火焰图功能，将函数与缓存未命中、分支预测错误等硬件性能事件关联起来。
另一个新增功能是挂钟时间分析。CPU 分析统计的是处理器实际占用时间，但很多时候服务 CPU 占用不高却响应缓慢，原因是线程在等待 IO、锁或者远程调用。挂钟时间分析可以把这类等待耗时可视化。
gProfiler 将数据采集与分析相分离。代理运行在各个主机上，而 gProfiler Performance Studio 负责聚合和可视化生成的性能分析数据。
性能分析数据存储在 S3 中，通过 SQS 进行异步索引，并存储在 ClickHouse 用于分析查询。React 前端提供火焰图交互浏览功能，聚合数据让工程师可以跨主机、服务和时间段比较性能分析结果。
Pinterest 和英特尔还针对生产环境对平台进行了加固，解决了代理资源消耗、磁盘占用、TB 级海量数据摄入等问题，然后才将其部署到整个集群。
gProfiler 所处的持续性能分析赛道竞争日益激烈。Parca 和 Grafana Pyroscope 使用 eBPF 及相关采样技术提供全集群范围的性能分析，而 Datadog 等商业平台则将持续性能分析与更广泛的观测能力相结合。
gProfiler 的差异化在于侧重系统级、多运行时性能分析，以及开源可扩展性。它不是要取代 perf 或 async-profiler 等工具，而是对它们进行编排。它还通过英特尔的工具链增加了硬件级性能分析能力。
英特尔的 VTune 能提供更深层次的处理器和应用性能分析，但它主要是作为性能工程工具设计的，而非云原生集群分析器。Pinterest 特别指出，正是这点差异，促使他们选择基于 gProfiler 进行构建，而不是去改造 VTune。
在小规模场景下，性能分析通常是工程师在出现性能问题时才会用的手段。而在 Pinterest 的业务规模下，等待工程师复现问题或手动对机器进行性能分析的代价太高了。持续性能分析提供了一个基线，而动态性能分析让团队可以在异常发生时进行针对性的排查。
通过在开源平台上整合运行时性能分析、系统行为和硬件性能数据，Pinterest 将性能分析打造为生产可观测性的又一层能力。

title: 智能体身份国际标准化：体系布局与研制实践｜AICon北京
summary:
当 Agent 真正进入企业流程，哪些工作可以交给 AI ？50 + 实战案例揭晓答案！
AI 正在从回答问题的辅助工具，走向理解目标、调用系统、完成任务的工作承担者。当 Agent 真正进入企业流程，问题不再是 “如何把 AI 做出来”，而是哪些工作可以交给 AI、结果如何验收、权限、成本与风险如何收住。随着大模型向推理、工具调用、多模态和长任务延伸，开发重心正从单次调用转向上下文、工具、执行环境与反馈回路的设计，Coding Agent 也从代码补全演进为能理解代码库、运行测试、完成复杂任务的工程协作者。OpenAI、Google Cloud、Anthropic 的最新实践共同指向一个结论：模型决定 Agent 能做什么，工程决定它能否真正进入生产、创造价值。
在这一背景下，2026 年 AICon 人工智能开发与应用大会 · 北京站将于 12 月 18–19 日，在北京新云南皇冠假日酒店举办。本届大会以探索 A 应用边界为主题，设置 13 大技术专题，覆盖大模型后训练、推理优化、Agent 工程、知识工程、智能体评测与安全、自进化系统、AI 软件交付、原生架构及组织变革等核心方向，汇聚一线技术专家，深入分享 AI 技术突破与企业规模化落地的真实实践。
信通院研究员张立锋已确认出席 “Agent Security｜身份、权限与行动安全” 专题，并发表题为《智能体身份国际标准化：体系布局与研制实践》的主题分享。当智能体开始代表用户访问数据、调用工具、执行交易，并将任务委托给其他智能体，身份管理需要回答的问题也随之扩展：正在执行任务的是哪个智能体，由谁开发和管理，代表谁行动，获得了什么授权，以及这些关系能否在跨平台协作中被验证和追溯。
围绕这些问题，国际标准化工作正在从既有数字身份技术向智能体场景延伸。ITU-T 已开展智能体身份数据模型、身份互操作等研究，IEEE 已布局基于可信数字身份的多智能体协作框架，IETF 正在推进智能体身份管理相关工作组草案。如何将这些工作与现有身份系统、凭证机制和应用协议衔接，仍需明确共同的术语、角色关系与技术边界。
张立锋的本次演讲，将系统梳理 ISO/IEC、ITU-T、IEEE、IETF、W3C 及其他相关组织的标准布局与研制进展，重点分析不同组织分别解决哪些问题、已有成果如何复用、哪些需求仍需补充。在此基础上，提出智能体身份的术语梳理与体系框架建议，结合相关项目分享研制实践，介绍 IEEE C/DTSC 数字信任标准委员会的工作布局。最后，讲解 IEEE 与 ITU-T 标准的立项路径、材料准备和参与方式，介绍其团队面向两类标准建设的相关标准工具箱，为参会者参与标准研制提供具体参考。
张立锋，中国信息通信研究院人工智能研究所研究员，IEEE 数字信任标准委员会秘书长、IEEE 信任科技行业连接组秘书长。主要从事端侧智能、数字身份等领域的技术研究与标准化工作，牵头完成十余项 ITU-T、IEEE 等国际标准及十余项行业标准的研制工作，参与多项国家重点研发计划项目，以通信作者身份发表多篇 SCI、EI 收录的期刊论文。
他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下：
演讲提纲
- 智能体身份的国际标准化布局 智能体身份的核心问题与标准化需求 ISO/IEC、ITU-T、IEEE 等组织的相关布局与代表性项目
- IETF：从工作负载身份到智能体认证与授权 WIMSE、OAuth 与智能体身份管理相关工作 AIMS 相关进展及其对用户、智能体与工具交互的支撑 委托关系、权限约束、凭证生命周期与审计的工程衔接
- W3C：标识符、可验证凭证与智能体身份探索 DID 与 VC 的核心机制及其在智能体身份中的应用 智能体协议与身份注册相关社区探索 凭证验证、信任判断与业务授权的衔接及边界
- 智能体身份体系框架与标准研制实践 智能体身份的术语、角色关系与参考框架 结合代表性项目介绍从场景需求到标准要求的提炼 IEEE C/DTSC 协作机制、IEEE 与 ITU-T 立项路径及工具箱简介
听众收益
- 建立国际标准布局视图：各组织研究重点、代表性成果、项目状态
- 厘清智能体身份与运行身份、用户身份、授权委托的区别与联系
- 获得平台建设的对照框架：从身份、凭证、权限、跨域信任、审计五个方面自查系统设计
- 了解标准研制与参与路径，掌握从业务问题提炼标准需求的方法
- 了解 IEEE 与 ITU-T 立项准备的关键事项与辅助工具
演讲亮点
- 按组织梳理、按问题对照，围绕身份表达、认证、委托、互操作与治理建立对应关系
- 同时覆盖基础成果与智能体专项进展，明确区分不同成熟度
- 以 F.DLT-DIS、P3763 等在研项目讲清"场景如何变成标准需求"
- 给出可讨论的术语与体系框架建议，而非罗列组织清单
- 把标准进展、立项方法与工具使用结合，听众可带走行动路径
除此之外，本次大会还策划了Post-Training Engineering｜数据、奖励与模型能力塑造、大模型推理与算力调度实践、Knowledge Engineering｜让 Agent 理解企业、Multi-Agent Systems、智能体评测与生产可靠性探索、Agent Security｜身份、权限与行动安全、AgentOps｜企业 Agent 全生命周期管理、Self-Evolving Agents｜从经验学习到可控进化、Agentic Software Engineering｜从代码生成到软件交付、Personal Agent、AI 原生架构的演进与治理、AI 时代的组织重构、AI × Industries ｜产业智能化等 13 个专题论坛，届时将有来自不同行业、不同领域、不同企业的资深专家在现场带来前沿技术洞察和一线实践经验。

张立锋，中国信息通信研究院人工智能研究所研究员，IEEE 数字信任标准委员会秘书长、IEEE 信任科技行业连接组秘书长。主要从事端侧智能、数字身份等领域的技术研究与标准化工作，牵头完成十余项 ITU-T、IEEE 等国际标准及十余项行业标准的研制工作，参与多项国家重点研发计划项目，以通信作者身份发表多篇 SCI、EI 收录的期刊论文。
他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下：
演讲提纲
- 智能体身份的国际标准化布局 智能体身份的核心问题与标准化需求 ISO/IEC、ITU-T、IEEE 等组织的相关布局与代表性项目
- IETF：从工作负载身份到智能体认证与授权 WIMSE、OAuth 与智能体身份管理相关工作 AIMS 相关进展及其对用户、智能体与工具交互的支撑 委托关系、权限约束、凭证生命周期与审计的工程衔接
- W3C：标识符、可验证凭证与智能体身份探索 DID 与 VC 的核心机制及其在智能体身份中的应用 智能体协议与身份注册相关社区探索 凭证验证、信任判断与业务授权的衔接及边界
- 智能体身份体系框架与标准研制实践 智能体身份的术语、角色关系与参考框架 结合代表性项目介绍从场景需求到标准要求的提炼 IEEE C/DTSC 协作机制、IEEE 与 ITU-T 立项路径及工具箱简介
听众收益
- 建立国际标准布局视图：各组织研究重点、代表性成果、项目状态
- 厘清智能体身份与运行身份、用户身份、授权委托的区别与联系
- 获得平台建设的对照框架：从身份、凭证、权限、跨域信任、审计五个方面自查系统设计
- 了解标准研制与参与路径，掌握从业务问题提炼标准需求的方法
- 了解 IEEE 与 ITU-T 立项准备的关键事项与辅助工具
演讲亮点
- 按组织梳理、按问题对照，围绕身份表达、认证、委托、互操作与治理建立对应关系
- 同时覆盖基础成果与智能体专项进展，明确区分不同成熟度
- 以 F.DLT-DIS、P3763 等在研项目讲清"场景如何变成标准需求"
- 给出可讨论的术语与体系框架建议，而非罗列组织清单
- 把标准进展、立项方法与工具使用结合，听众可带走行动路径
除此之外，本次大会还策划了Post-Training Engineering｜数据、奖励与模型能力塑造、大模型推理与算力调度实践、Knowledge Engineering｜让 Agent 理解企业、Multi-Agent Systems、智能体评测与生产可靠性探索、Agent Security｜身份、权限与行动安全、AgentOps｜企业 Agent 全生命周期管理、Self-Evolving Agents｜从经验学习到可控进化、Agentic Software Engineering｜从代码生成到软件交付、Personal Agent、AI 原生架构的演进与治理、AI 时代的组织重构、AI × Industries ｜产业智能化等 13 个专题论坛，届时将有来自不同行业、不同领域、不同企业的资深专家在现场带来前沿技术洞察和一线实践经验。

title: 亚马逊云科技推出 TorchNeuron，可以直接在 AWS Trainium 上运行 PyTorch 模型，无需任何修改
summary:
在最近举行的 2026 年 PyTorch 北美大会上，亚马逊云科技推出了 TorchNeuron——这是一个原生 PyTorch 后端，可以让开发者在几乎无需修改代码的情况下，在 AWS Trainium AI 芯片上运行现有的 PyTorch 代码。
除了减少工程工作量外，TorchNeuron 还允许企业在训练和推理工作负载之间共享硬件容量，并在非高峰时段将资源从推理任务重新分配到训练任务。
亚马逊云科技表示，只需要进行一次配置更改即可切换硬件，在迁移至 Trainium 时不需要重写和重新验证模型。
如今，85% 的人工智能研究人员和开发者都在使用 PyTorch 编写代码。此前，能够运行这些代码的硬件远比代码本身的限制要多，要扩展到新的芯片，就意味着需要重写并重新验证那些耗时数月才臻于完美的代码。
根据 TorchNeuron 的文档，当通过 torch.accelerator 利用 PyTorch 的自动设备检测功能时，唯一需要做出的改动就是将 .to(‘cuda’) 替换为 .to(‘neuron’)。该后端还原生支持分布式训练和 PyTorch 并行 API，包括 DDP、FSDP2、DTensor 等。此外，TorchNeuron 还通过 torch_neuronx.Stream 和 torch_neuronx.Event 为 Torch 流和事件提供原生支持。
Amazon Annapurna Labs 副总裁 Colin Brace ——他领导着 TorchNeuron 开发团队——强调，为了确保开发者在采用新后端时能够获得流畅的开发体验，他的团队对 10 万个最受欢迎的模型和 800 多种机器学习架构进行了验证。
此外，TorchNeuron 还允许开发者和研究人员使用 Neuron 内核接口（NKI）来开发、优化和执行自定义运算符：
开发者可以通过在模型代码中直接调用对性能至关重要的 NKI 内核，来替代一系列标准的 PyTorch 操作（ATen 操作），从而获得比自适应即时执行（Adaptive Eager）和 torch.compile 更精细的性能控制。
针对亚马逊云科技在 LinkedIn 上的公告，Liner Notes Consulting 首席执行官 Yasuo Maeda 指出：
真正的考验在于开发者能否在生产环境中实现具有竞争力的性能和总拥有成本。AI 基础设施的竞争不仅在于谁能制造出最好的芯片，还在于谁能让这些芯片在规模化应用时更易于使用。
同样，用户 Pratham pratham 也强调，虽然降低迁移门槛对于避免加速器锁定至关重要，但真正的考验在于针对特定工作负载的性能、每 token 成本以及可重复性。
亚马逊云科技还强调，TorchNeuron 已经被多家机构采用，其中包括将该技术用于语音 AI 推理的 Cartesia，以及探索其在药物靶点识别和药物发现领域应用的利伯脑发育研究所。
亚马逊云科技发布 TorchNeuron 的消息紧随谷歌推出 TorchTPU 之后——TorchTPU 是谷歌为其 TPU 硬件开发的原生 PyTorch 后端。
声明：本文为 InfoQ 翻译，未经许可禁止转载。

title: 智能体 AI 架构：当前挑战与未来机遇
summary:
大多数软件工程师和架构师对微服务和云原生架构早已耳熟能详，多年来也一直参与构建基于这些架构的系统。基于微服务的系统通常由数十、数百甚至数千个服务组成，负责不同类型的数据处理任务——API 端点、数据管道、后台工作流，以及各类中间场景——但它们都有一个共同点：按照代码确定的逻辑或基于从数据存储中检索到的数据来处理数据。这并不意味着这类系统很简单，恰恰相反，它们可能十分复杂。但即使它们很复杂，人们仍然可以用确定性的方式对它们进行推理，这有助于定义和界定功能范围、实现、测试变更和运维系统，哪怕遇到基础设施或应用层面的故障。
但这一切即将迎来改变。事实上，未来软件系统中有相当一部分仍将保持确定性，和我们如今熟悉的形态相近。但用不了多久，大量正在设计和交付的 IT 系统将利用基于 AI 的解决方案来驱动面向用户的功能。对绝大多数（甚至全部）架构师和工程师而言，他们必须适应 IT 行业全新的现实。
AI 进入软件架构，核心驱动力来自 AI 带来的全新能力，这类能力对于知识工作者使用的产品尤为有用。在过去，IT 系统专注于存储、处理数据，并通过 API 和用户界面提供数据。与此同时，人类负责相当一部分数据管理工作，运用业务规则、流程、团队内部沉淀的隐性经验以及个人判断力开展工作。客观来说，其中一部分（甚至很大一部分）智能被直接构建到 IT 系统中，用以提高生产力，尤其是在业务规模化扩张的关键阶段。借助 AI 能力，软件系统可以从操作原始数据转变为操作知识，从而将 IT 的角色从单纯的数据管理和处理职能提升为在知识层面支撑业务运转、赋能终端用户。
我们很难判断基于 AI 的方案会在多大程度上主导下一代软件系统。但种种迹象表明，它带来的影响会极其深远，足以催生一种全新的软件架构：由 AI 驱动大量功能模块，让使用这套下一代系统构建产品的人工作效率大幅提升。智能体 AI 架构是指大规模使用智能体 AI 系统、以充分发挥生成式 AI（以及其他）模型能力为目标的软件架构。这类架构建立在微服务和云原生架构之上，并加入了智能体 AI 能力。
智能体 AI 系统的兴起
智能体 AI 并不是全新概念，但也尚未发展成熟。过去几年，智能体 AI 系统已经从简单的单智能体解决方案，演变为链式结构，再到图结构和多智能体系统（MAS）——多个智能体按照不同的拓扑结构协同工作。这一领域仍处在快速发展阶段，未来必然会涌现出更复杂的应用场景。不过要注意，不同的协作策略或拓扑结构适合特定的场景，很多时候，选择更简洁的方案反而更有利。
智能体依靠合适的上下文充分发挥与之交互的大语言模型的能力。上下文方案也在迭代：从最早的预设提示词开始，之后逐步演进为动态上下文——上下文信息来自其他智能体的输出、上下文传递或是通过检索增强生成（RAG）从外部数据源拉取的数据。
当来自不同来源的上下文信息不断累积，开始出现推理能力下降的问题，工程师摸索出了新的上下文管理方式，上下文工程由此成为一项独立的实践。渐进式上下文披露（Progressive Context Disclosure）技术可以进一步优化上下文准备步骤：智能体能够根据用户提示词选择性地把详细信息加载到上下文窗口中。
由于 LLM 的上下文窗口存在大小限制，上下文工程的作用在于确保所使用的上下文能够最大化模型产生期望结果的可能性，或至少最大限度地降低因上下文模糊或不充分而产生幻觉的几率。有效的上下文工程需要上下文管理来存储、优化和复用上下文元素，以供后续的智能体调用。
最近，面向 AI 智能体的记忆系统也应运而生，进一步增强了上下文编辑能力。这些系统对不同类型的长期记忆（情景记忆、语义记忆、程序记忆）进行组织和查询，让智能体能够用过去的经验/决策、相关事实/定义、规则或习得的行为来补充上下文。
上下文工程已成为智能体 AI 系统的基础性架构关注点。随着构建和运营基于 AI 的产品所需的要求和期望不断增长，它也必将持续演化。
智能体 AI 已经发展出一系列专有的通信协议。这一过程在很大程度上是由智能体开发的复杂性、标准化的需求以及改进互操作性的需求所驱动的：
- Agent2Agent 协议（A2A）——专为多智能体系统设计，实现 AI 智能体之间的互操作。
- 模型上下文协议（MCP）——专注于 AI 智能体与外部服务（数据库、工具等）之间的通信。
从智能体 AI 系统到智能体 AI 架构
要让智能体 AI 系统产生价值，就需要将其集成到更大的企业架构中。在企业环境中，可以通过以下方式集成智能体 AI 系统：
- 将智能体嵌入到对外暴露 API（HTTP/GRPC）的微服务中；
- 把智能体作为 MCP 工具或是基于 A2A 协议进行调用；
- 让智能体微服务消费来自异步通道（队列/主题）的消息。
大型企业级架构可能包含许多专门的智能体 AI 系统。由于 AI 智能体可以通过 MCP 直接访问数据库、服务/API 或任意数据源，因此有必要按照领域驱动设计（DDD）的思路把智能体的交互范围限制在限界上下文内。在大型的架构中限制智能体 AI 系统的作用域可以减少相距遥远或不相关的组件和数据源之间的耦合，让工程团队能够维护更具内聚性的区域，而不会产生过多的依赖或在引入变更时造成过大的影响。
图 1 描绘了一个简化的架构，其中包含两个限界上下文，每个上下文都嵌入了一个包含多个智能体（A）的智能体 AI 系统和其他微服务（S）。智能体仅使用本地数据源和服务进行上下文扩展，降低了与更大软件系统其他部分的耦合。
智能体 AI 系统的性能与可扩展性
云原生软件架构的可扩展性已经被充分理解，架构师和工程师已经搭建、运维这类系统很长时间了。但智能体 AI 系统并非如此：大模型调用延迟更高，复杂的多智能体系统还可能进一步增加处理耗时。评估智能体 AI 系统性能不能只依靠吞吐量、延迟、错误率这类传统指标。
谷歌和麻省理工学院的研究人员发表了一篇介绍多智能体系统扩展框架的论文。研究团队测试了多种多智能体协调策略，每种策略都有若干配置参数，包括 LLM 调用次数、智能体数量和每个智能体的交互次数。研究人员得出结论：最佳的协调策略取决于具体任务——金融推理场景更适合中心化编排，网页导航类场景则去中心化策略效果更好。
谷歌和 MIT 的研究结果表明，在智能体 AI 领域不存在一刀切的方案，构建复杂解决方案的团队必须反复试验，通过实证确定最适合其任务的智能体协调策略。
智能体 AI 的安全挑战
将智能体 AI 纳入分布式系统架构会显著改变安全模型。智能体 AI 带来了额外的安全威胁，主要集中在智能体运行时、工具服务器（MCP 或其他）以及模型服务商侧。例如，AI 智能体可能容易受到提示词注入、指令混淆或工具输出投毒的攻击，从而导致非预期的行为或泄露它们可访问的数据。此外，使用外部 LLM 模型还会引入数据属地、数据保留或数据使用合规等风险。
现有的访问控制模型经过数十年的打磨，但并不适合智能体——智能体实际上既不能被视为人类用户，也不能被视为后端服务。Auth0 高级开发者 Cameron Pavey 最近提出了一种专门针对 AI 智能体的新权限模型。他认为，常规（非 AI）后端服务通常更受信任，因为它们是确定性的、可审计的，而且认证会话和用户界面会对用户形成约束。相比之下，智能体可以在用户不知情或未明确许可的情况下自主触发包含其他智能体、工具调用的多步骤工作流。
Pavey 提出使用能力范围权限和任务范围凭证作为解决智能体权限问题、采用细粒度授权系统进行分层执行的关键步骤。
值得一提的是，安全领域并不是第一次出现这种重大变化。当年微服务、云原生架构兴起时，我们也看到了这一领域的转变，导致了访问控制机制和协议的重塑，以及 JWT 和 OAuth 等如今司空见惯的技术的出现。
可观测性
智能体 AI 系统具备非确定性，因此可观测性是有效构建、增强、排查故障和运维这类系统的关键。
团队应力求覆盖现代可观测性平台的全部核心维度：
- 日志——使用结构化日志，记录决策及其理由和证据；包含关联 ID；清除个人身份信息。
- 指标——评估输出质量、延迟、成本；为性能和预算创建 SLO 仪表盘。
- 追踪——追踪任务/步骤（规划、工具、验证）；包含关联 ID。
- 告警——对性能下降、延迟突增、异常情况进行告警。
- 运行手册——维护一套定期评审的运行手册。
微服务、云原生与智能体 AI 架构的融合
尽管智能体 AI 有望成为未来 IT 产品和服务的主导力量，但我们不能指望瞬间完成切换。在未来的许多年里，我们今天所熟知的分布式系统架构将与下一代架构共存，就像面向服务架构（SOA）用了数年时间逐步被微服务替代一样。
此外，鉴于智能体 AI 尚处于相对初级的阶段，这一领域需要一些时间才能发展成熟并获得广泛采用，过渡会循序渐进，新的设计模式、最佳实践、配套技术也会不断涌现，从而进一步推动普及。
最后，并非所有产品或业务流程都需要智能体 AI，或者在部分场景下使用 AI 不具备经济可行性。某些行业或某类产品/系统可能无法像其他行业一样快速从 AI 中受益。从这个意义上说，微服务和云原生架构将以某种形式继续存在。
从微服务与云原生到智能体 AI 平台
随着智能体 AI 逐步成为行业主流，行业内的成熟度和采用度不断提升，我预计很多当前需要定制开发的组件和方案，未来会封装成通用平台能力。这些平台将支持多智能体系统的交付和运维，并且能够把智能体系统集成到更大规模的企业架构中。
尤其是智能体 AI 基础组件：智能体记忆、资产注册、安全护栏、编排能力，以及配套的可观测性和运维能力，都会成为智能体 AI 平台的内置能力——无论是自研，还是由供应商或云服务商提供。
目前已有若干可供开发者使用的智能体 AI 平台/框架，包括 LangChain（含 LangGraph）、CrewAI、Azure AI Foundry、Google Agent SDK (ADK)、Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway。
这一过程将遵循与微服务架构相同的路径：企业落地新架构产生大量需求，催生内部自建运维方案，之后逐步被托管式商业化产品替代。
智能体 AI 架构的未来
行业正处于重大变革的前夜，智能体 AI 架构很有可能在未来数年乃至数十年内成为分布式系统的主导架构。这并不意味着微服务和云原生架构将过时，相反，它们将构成下一代系统的基础，在这些系统中，AI 驱动着绝大部分用户体验。架构师和工程师今天所熟悉的内容，将成为交付 AI 产品和服务的基础——这些产品和服务融合了数据、知识和基于计算的推理。
这里所描述的转变将提高众多行业知识工作者的生产力，并改善其使用体验。它不仅会极大地重塑 IT 行业，还会深刻改变整个现代社会。
我们目前仍处在早期阶段，创新层出不穷，目标持续迭代，大量实践、试错与学习正在发生，但前路无疑充满机遇。
